newsitem.title: UK: Release of tanker held in Venezuela seen delayed.
newsitem.headline: Release of tanker held in Venezuela seen delayed.

text.p: Hopes that a legal order might be made this week or early next to release a detained Greek tanker and its master from detention in Venezuela appear to have been dashed, a tanker owners' representative said Friday.
On Thursday Venezuela's attorney general officially announced the suspension of charges against the Nissos Amorgos relating to the arrest of the ship made by the Caracas court.
The Greek-owned 89,427 dwt tanker has been held since she spilled around 25,000 barrels of oil in Venezuela's lake Maracaibo shipping channel on February 28.

However, a representative for the independent tanker owners' organisation, Intertanko, said indications that a local Cabimas Court would also issue a decision on the vessel by early next week looked remote.
The Intertanko spokesman said the Cabimas judge had indicated a decision would be made on Monday June 16, but that on that day the court had announced the judge would be away for a week.
It is believed a request had been sent from Caracas to the local court ahead of the official announcement.
The Intertanko spokesman added that next Monday and Tuesday are holidays in Venezuela.
It is now hoped that the attorney general's actions will effect the release of the ship and the master later next week, the Intertanko spokesman added.

Intertanko and the Nissos Amorgos' owner have argued that as Venezuela is a signatory to international conventions covering compensation from oil spills, there is no reason why the ship and master should be detained.

The Civil Liabilities Convention covering compensation for oil spills covers an initial $ 7.2 million and a second fund provides for a further $83 million if necessary. Fishermens' unions in Venezuela have filed a suit for at least $130 million.

At a meeting at the beginning of this week of the International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund (IOPCF) executive committee, the Venezuelan delegation reportedly stated that a revised guarantee was being negotiated with the ships' owner and its protection and indemnity (P&I) insurer which should have allowed the vessel to sail this week.
At the meeting several other signatory countries to the pollution conventions declared that member states should implement the funds' requirements as a matter of priority.
Meanwhile the Venezuelan union of pilots and mariners, UNPOMAR, has responded to a request from the Pan-Hellenic Seamen's Federation for help to release the ship's captain.

UNPOMAR president Pedro Jose Ramirez Hernandez wrote that the masters he represents are concerned about security of navigation on the Maracaibo lake. He added that the pilot of the Nissos Amorgos at the time of her grounding has also been detained.

Intertanko has also now approached the International Maritime Organisation in an attempt to widen support for the release of the Nissos Amorgos. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
